gen-dafont-disorder-gf-savate: Disorder's tails and terminals carry full stem weight, with no swelling at the joins, so its big lowercase looks blunt and raw. Savate's open curves and faint pen pressure keep paragraphs gentle.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Raw and chaotic, Disorder holds one constant stroke width throughout. Schibsted Grotesk has big open e and a shapes with tall bowls and unclosed terminals, so paragraphs feel approachable and light on the eye.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-sen: Disorder spaces its raw, chaotic letters well apart, with a high x-height that makes the lowercase look big. And Sen's tall lowercase, traced in one constant line, gives that wildness a steady partner on the page.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-sintony: Wire-cut and unruly, Disorder spaces its glyphs well apart, with no swelling where curves meet stems and a big-looking lowercase. Sintony's chunky, tall midzone keeps the page smooth beside it.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-sofia-sans: Sofia Sans keeps every stroke uniform, with rounded letters left clearly open and tall lowercase like cut acrylic stencil pieces. Sofia Sans holds steady while Disorder runs loose, and that gap is the pair's best trait.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-sofia-sans-semi-c: Disorder spaces its glyphs well apart and draws its curves without swelling at the stems, making lowercase look big. Sofia Sans Semi Condensed brings a stencil-cut line, steady against the mess.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-sono: Sono has tall lowercase, wide default spacing and an a with its mouth left ajar, all easygoing beside Disorder's ballpoint-plain line. Disorder makes the noise and Sono keeps things readable.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-stack-sans-headli: Stack Sans Headline keeps a monoline skeleton and a deep middle band, with wide gaps that hold tiny sizes crisp. But beside Disorder, all raw and scattered, it feels settled.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-stack-sans-notch: Stack Sans Notch reads big-bodied and open, its curves easy to see into and its strokes uniform like rod stock. Disorder supplies the mess, and this one keeps order.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-stack-sans-text: Chaotic and raw, Disorder scatters its glyphs wide, with a high x-height that makes its lowercase look big. Disorder grabs attention; Stack Sans Text carries the words with a marker-like line.
